tasks.notes: `waitInfraBackoff` (fleet/run-engine.mjs) keeps the event loop alive with `fs.watch(runDir)` because the global constraint forces the `setTimeout` to be unref'd — but when `fs.watch` throws (inotify watch/instance limit exhausted, EMFILE/ENOSPC, or a runDir removed underneath the engine) the `catch` sets `hold = null` and the unref'd timer becomes the only pending work. That is exactly the condition the block's own comment measured: node exits 13 with an unsettled top-level await, so instead of retrying the judgment the whole run dies silently mid-backoff, without even the fail-closed finding a second null would have produced. The fallback should be another ref'd non-timer handle rather than nothing; a `MessageChannel` port with a listener is a global in the supported node versions and closes the same way.; The driver's REFEREE line records `Produces: infraBackoffMs` as declared-but-not-exported. Nothing in the diff can settle that: the task's own Context defines it as a run argument (`args.infraBackoffMs`, "the sims pass 0"), not a module export, so no `export` in fleet/run-engine.mjs would be correct here. It is implemented as the `infraBackoffMs` binding in `runEngine` and exercised by legs (a) ('x' -> 60000) and (j) (300). The defect is the Interfaces slot naming an args key where the linker resolves symbols; no edit inside this tree answers it, and it blocks nothing.; Global constraint (prose, no `Check:` the driver ran) — "no timer that holds the process open (`unref` every `setTimeout` the backoff creates)". `waitInfraBackoff` (fleet/run-engine.mjs, the hunk at PATCH lines 78-86) does unref the `setTimeout`, then substitutes a **ref'd** `fs.watch(runDir)` handle to keep the loop alive for exactly the same interval. Read literally the constraint is met; read for what the parenthetical is aimed at — a backoff being the reason a finished process is still alive — a ref'd handle held for the full 60 s is the same effect under a different handle type. It is not blocking: the divergence is disclosed in the comment above it with the measured rationale (exit 13, unsettled top-level await), the handle is closed in the timer callback so nothing outlives the re-dispatch, and the sims run at 0/300 ms. Two things to consider anyway: (1) the failure branch is silent — if `fs.watch` throws (runDir gone, EMFILE, no inotify) `hold` stays `null` and the process can exit mid-backoff, after the attempt-1 `judgmentCalls` entry and `driver:infra-retry` event have already been written, so the record shows a re-dispatch that never happened; a `log()` on that branch would make it legible. (2) A ref'd `setTimeout` cleared in the resolve path expresses the same lifetime more directly, but is the thing the constraint's text forbids — if that is the shape the plan actually wanted, it is worth saying so in the plan rather than routing around the wording.; fleet/run-engine.mjs, the reviewer-pair hunk (PATCH lines 159-166): the two retries are sequential — `if (r1 === null) await retryInfraNull(...)` then `if (r2 === null) await retryInfraNull(...)`. An overload storm is correlated, so both halves of a pair dying together is the likely case, and that path now waits 2 x INFRA_BACKOFF_MS (120 s) serially before the second re-dispatch. M7 only pins the one-null shape, so this is not a criterion miss. Fix shape: compute the two retry thunks and `await Promise.all([...])` so the single backoff is shared, e.g. `const [n1, n2] = await Promise.all([r1 === null ? retryInfraNull(opts1.label, scope, () => timedReview(reviewPrompt, opts1)) : r1, r2 === null ? retryInfraNull(opts2.label, scope, () => timedReview(reviewPrompt, opts2)) : r2])`. Keeps the leg (i) assertions (each label dispatched exactly twice, the answering half exactly once) true.; fleet/run-engine.mjs: `const kept = (impl.status === 'DONE' || impl.status === 'DONE_WITH_CONCERNS') && hasCoordinates(impl)` is now computed identically in two adjacent branches — the rejected-examiner lane (BASE line 1520) and the new fulfilled-null lane (PATCH line 126). It is the same subtle condition in both, and the two must stay in step. Hoisting one `const kept = ...` above the `if (examSettled.status === 'rejected')` / `else if (examReady && ex === null)` chain removes the duplicate without touching either branch's behavior.; REFEREE reports `Produces: infraBackoffMs — declared, not exported`. The diff is right and the plan's Interfaces slot is what is off: M1 defines the knob as `args.infraBackoffMs`, a `runEngine` options field read at PATCH line 42, so it is by construction not a module export and cannot resolve as one at HEAD. `INFRA_BACKOFF_MS`, the symbol that genuinely is an export, is exported at PATCH line 19 and pinned by leg (a)'s namespace import. No edit inside FILES answers the arithmetic line; the Interfaces slot would have to stop using the `Produces:` grammar for an options field.; Produces: `infraBackoffMs` — fleet/run-engine.mjs: declared, not exported; fleet/tests/test_run_engine_infra_retry.mjs: declared, not exported; concern: Disclosure (not a scope escape): the backoff creates its setTimeout and unrefs it as the Global Constraint requires, but an unref'd timer is also no reason for the loop to keep running — measured, node exits mid-run with code 13 ("unsettled top-level await") when the wait is the only pending work, which would kill any sim that exercises a non-zero backoff. So the wait also holds one ref'd NON-timer handle (fs.watch on runDir) that is closed the instant the timer fires: every setTimeout is still unref'd and nothing outlives the re-dispatch. If a reviewer reads the constraint as forbidding any keep-alive at all, the alternative is a backoff that cannot actually elapse.

completenessFindings.detail: Task 1 / Claim, fleet/run-engine.mjs:1150-1158 (`waitInfraBackoff`): the ref'd handle that keeps the event loop alive for the backoff is `fs.watch(runDir, …)`, and its failure is swallowed (`catch { hold = null }`), leaving only the unref'd `setTimeout`. On a host where `fs.watch` throws (inotify watch limit exhausted, an unsupported filesystem), the critic's backoff is the only pending work at that point in the run, so node exits out from under the wait — the exit-13 'unsettled top-level await' the block's own comment records as measured. The outcome is then worse than BASE for the very case the Claim addresses: instead of the fail-closed report with `gitVerified` withheld, the run ends mid-backoff with no report at all. The one-retry semantics are correct; only the liveness fallback is unguarded (e.g. no ref'd fallback and no judgment call noting the hold could not be taken).

Task 1 / Claim, fleet/run-engine.mjs:2116-2123 (the pair lane): the two halves' re-dispatches are sequential — `if (r1 === null) await retryInfraNull(...)` then `if (r2 === null) await retryInfraNull(...)` — and each `retryInfraNull` waits the full `infraBackoffMs` before its own re-ask. When an infra storm kills both halves of a pair (the correlated case, and the one this feature exists for), the task serially waits two backoffs, 120 s at the default `INFRA_BACKOFF_MS`, where one concurrent wait would do; the second half's re-ask also starts a full backoff after the first half's has already elapsed. M7 specifies only the one-dead-half shape, so this is not a contract miss — behaviour stays correct (either half still null falls to the `AGENT_NULL` throw, the park and the barrier retry) — but the doubled wall clock on the both-dead path is worth an issue.
